answers.value: All in-force life policies within the reinstatement window whose reinstatement request is under evaluation for whether underwriting approval and/or new evidence of insurability is required; scope = one policy per case, keyed on the policy record in the Guidewire PolicyCenter/ALIP policy administration system (PAS).

The lapse-to-request interval for the specific policy (from cancellation/lapse date to the reinstatement request date); reinstatement rules are applied as of the request date and the elapsed months drive the evidence-of-insurability tier.

Policy status = Lapsed/Cancelled, lapse date, product/plan code, face amount, elapsed months since lapse, and any prior underwriting class are populated and valid in PAS before the requirement tier is determined; a blank lapse date or face amount blocks the assessment.

The evidence-requirement decision reconciles to the reinstatement rules matrix: <6 months = simplified/no new evidence, 6-12 months = reinstatement application + short-form health statement, >12 months = full evidence of insurability; the tier selected must match the elapsed-months band with 0 exceptions.

The requirement determination memo is saved to the policy record in PAS and exported to the GRC platform under /underwriting/reinstatement/<policy-no>/ with timestamp and version label; retained per the life records retention schedule (7 years).

Cases that fall outside the standard matrix (e.g. impaired-risk history, contestable-period overlap) are logged as reinstatement exceptions in the underwriting workstation with disposition (approve with evidence / decline / refer to Medical) and routed to the Senior Underwriter.
The requirement tier on a sampled case traces to the lapse date and elapsed months shown on the PAS policy screen and the reinstatement rules matrix version cited in the memo.

Reinstatement workflow status advances Lapsed -> Reinstatement Under Review -> Evidence Requested/Not Required, matching the requirement determination; status in the underwriting workstation aligns to the decision recorded.
Lapse date, request-received date and evidence-due date are populated and internally consistent (request date after lapse date; evidence-due date = request date + 30 days) in PAS.
Quarterly sample of 25 reinstatement determinations across products, drawn from PAS reinstatement-review queue for the quarter.

PASS = requirement tier matches the elapsed-months band and product rule and is documented with sign-off; FAIL = wrong tier applied, missing health evidence where required, or no documented rationale. Target >= 98% conformance.
Failures are returned to the owning Underwriter for correction within 2 business days, re-evidence ordered if under-required, and repeat errors escalated to the Underwriting Manager for coaching.

Acceptance = every reinstatement case has a documented evidence-requirement determination tied to the current rules matrix version, an approver sign-off, and (where >12 months) full evidence of insurability on file before approval.
Evidence lands in the GRC platform folder /underwriting/reinstatement/<policy-no>/ and on the PAS policy record; sample-review results retained in the underwriting QA workbook.

answers.value: All outstanding premium (unpaid premium plus any interest/late charges per policy terms) that must be collected as a precondition to reinstating the lapsed policy; scope = one policy per case, driven from the billing/commission platform receivable balance.
From lapse date through the reinstatement request date: all premium due during the lapsed period is aggregated as the reinstatement amount owed as of the request date.

Premium-in-arrears amount, interest/late fee, payment method and cleared-funds date are populated and valid in the billing/commission platform; reinstatement cannot proceed until the receivable shows a zero balance with cleared funds.

Sum of payments applied reconciles to the reinstatement amount owed (arrears + interest) with delta = 0; the billing receivable balance nets to zero and matches the amount cited in the reinstatement determination.

Payment receipt and reconciled receivable are stored on the PAS policy record and exported to the GRC platform under /underwriting/reinstatement/<policy-no>/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.

Partial payments, dishonored/NSF payments or disputed amounts are logged as billing exceptions in the billing/commission platform with disposition (hold reinstatement / request balance / refund) and the case is kept in Pending-Premium status until cleared.
The collected amount on a sampled case traces to the billing receivable transactions and the payment gateway/receipt reference recorded in the billing platform.
Billing status advances Arrears -> Payment Received -> Cleared, and only a Cleared status permits the reinstatement workflow to move to reactivation.
Payment date and funds-cleared date are populated and precede the reinstatement effective date; no reinstatement effective date is set before the cleared-funds date.
Quarterly sample of 25 reinstated policies drawn from the billing platform reinstatement-payment transactions for the quarter.

PASS = full arrears plus interest collected with cleared funds before reinstatement effective date and receivable at zero; FAIL = reinstatement effected with an open balance or uncollected interest. Target 100% (control is preventive).

Any reinstatement found effected with an open balance is reversed or the balance is billed and collected within 2 business days; root cause logged and escalated to the Underwriting Manager if a control override occurred.
Acceptance = reinstatement amount owed fully collected and cleared, receivable balance zero, and payment evidence linked to the policy record before the reinstatement is issued.
Payment evidence in the billing/commission platform and the GRC folder /underwriting/reinstatement/<policy-no>/; sample results in the underwriting QA workbook.

answers.value: Confirmation that elapsed time since cancellation/lapse falls within the reinstatement eligibility window per the policy contract and the applicable state reinstatement statute; scope = one policy per case, evaluated against the PAS lapse date.

Interval from cancellation/lapse date to reinstatement request date; the maximum window is typically 3 years for life (contract-specific) or the state-mandated period, measured as of the request date.
Lapse date, request date, issue state, product/contract reinstatement clause and computed elapsed months are populated and valid in PAS; the eligibility clause version is cited before confirmation.

Computed elapsed months reconcile to the difference between request date and lapse date, and the eligibility determination (eligible/ineligible) matches the contract window and the state maximum, whichever is more favorable to the insured; delta between manual and system calc = 0.

The eligibility confirmation (window, cited clause, state rule, decision) is stored on the PAS policy record and exported to the GRC folder /underwriting/reinstatement/<policy-no>/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.

Cases outside the window are logged as ineligible with disposition (decline reinstatement / offer new-business application) in the underwriting workstation; borderline dates near the cutoff are referred to the Senior Underwriter.
The eligibility decision on a sampled case traces to the lapse date on the PAS screen, the cited contract clause and the state reinstatement rule reference.
Reinstatement status is set to Eligible or Ineligible-Window and blocks downstream reactivation when Ineligible; status aligns with the confirmed window decision.
Lapse date and request date are valid and consistent (request after lapse) and the computed window end date is present and used in the eligibility check.
Quarterly sample of 25 reinstatement eligibility confirmations from the PAS reinstatement queue for the quarter, spanning multiple issue states.

PASS = elapsed months correctly computed and compared to the correct contract/state window with matching decision; FAIL = miscomputed elapsed time, wrong window applied, or eligible/ineligible decision inconsistent with the rule. Target >= 99%.
Failures are corrected within 2 business days; ineligible-but-reinstated cases are reversed and the insured offered a new-business path; systemic window-logic errors raised to Product/Compliance.
Effective dating: eligibility is judged as of the request date against the lapse date; the reinstatement effective date is never earlier than the cleared-premium date.

Field definitions from the PAS data dictionary: lapse_date, request_date, elapsed_months, contract_reinstatement_window, state_max_window, eligibility_decision. Control total = elapsed_months recomputed from dates reconciles to the system value with 0 variance.

Restated premium and ceded premium reconcile to the reinstated policy: billing receivable, ledger premium and reinsurance cession all reflect the same reinstated in-force amount; delta across billing and reinsurance systems = 0.

answers.value: Reactivation of the lapsed policy in the policy administration system with the correct reinstatement effective date and confirmation of coverage continuity; scope = one policy per case, keyed on the PAS policy record.

Reactivation occurs once premium is cleared and eligibility/underwriting is confirmed; the effective date is set no earlier than the cleared-premium date and the coverage-continuity check spans lapse date to effective date.

Reinstatement effective date, coverage terms, sum insured, beneficiary and any revised exclusions are populated and valid in PAS at reactivation; the policy status flips to In-Force only when all required fields pass validation.

Reactivated policy attributes reconcile to the pre-lapse policy plus any reinstatement changes; sum insured, premium mode and coverage codes match with 0 unexplained differences and the effective date equals the approved reinstatement date.

The reactivation transaction (before/after policy image) is retained on the PAS record and exported to the GRC folder /underwriting/reinstatement/<policy-no>/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.

Reactivation errors (wrong effective date, coverage-gap misstatement, failed continuity check) are logged as exceptions in the underwriting workstation with disposition (correct-and-reissue / reverse) and routed to the Senior Underwriter.
The reactivated policy attributes on a sampled case trace to the pre-lapse policy image in PAS and the approved reinstatement transaction record.
Policy status advances Reinstatement Approved -> Reactivated/In-Force only after the effective date and coverage terms pass validation; status aligns to the reactivation decision.
Reinstatement effective date and reactivation transaction date are populated and consistent (effective date >= cleared-premium date), and lapse/effective dates bound the coverage-continuity window.

The PAS reinstatement/reactivation transaction rules and effective-dating configuration are the approved production version; any change to reinstatement date logic goes through change control before use.

Sensitivity: reactivations where the effective date differs from the request date by more than the standard grace, or where coverage terms changed, are flagged for independent re-check before the status flips to In-Force.
Materiality: any face-amount or coverage-term difference between the pre-lapse and reactivated policy is material and must be documented and approved; immaterial cosmetic differences are noted only.
Quarterly sample of 25 reactivated policies drawn from the PAS reinstatement transaction log.

Acceptance = policy status In-Force with the correct reinstatement effective date, documented coverage continuity, and a retained before/after transaction image approved by the Senior Underwriter.
Evidence in the PAS transaction log and the GRC folder /underwriting/reinstatement/<policy-no>/; sample results in the underwriting QA workbook.

answers.value: Review of any loss activity, claims or material risk changes that occurred during the lapsed period before the policy is reinstated; scope = one policy per case, evaluated against claims history in the claims management platform and loss-history reports.
The lapsed period only: from lapse/cancellation date to reinstatement request date; claims, incidents and risk changes with a date-of-loss inside this window are in scope.

Claims history, loss-run, any reported incidents and material risk-change disclosures for the lapsed window are populated and valid; the review cannot be completed until a loss-history check for the period is on file.

The number and value of losses considered reconcile to the claims platform loss-run for the lapsed period; the review conclusion (no material change / adverse loss activity) matches the loss data with 0 unreconciled claims.

The loss-activity review memo and loss-run extract are stored on the PAS policy record and exported to the GRC folder /underwriting/reinstatement/<policy-no>/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.

Adverse loss activity or new material risk during the lapse is logged as an exception with disposition (decline reinstatement / reinstate with revised terms or exclusion / refer) in the underwriting workstation and routed to the Senior Underwriter.
Losses cited in the review trace to claim records in the claims management platform and the loss-history report for the lapsed period.
Reinstatement status reflects the loss-review outcome (Clear / Refer-Adverse-Loss); an adverse finding blocks straight-through reinstatement and forces referral.
Date-of-loss on each considered claim falls within the lapse window; lapse date and request date bound the review period and are validated for consistency.
Quarterly sample of 25 reinstatement loss-activity reviews drawn from the PAS reinstatement queue for the quarter.
PASS = loss-history for the full lapse window reviewed, findings documented, and adverse activity referred/actioned; FAIL = no loss check, incomplete window, or adverse loss ignored. Target >= 98%.
Failures are re-worked within 2 business days with a completed loss-history check; reinstatements approved despite unreviewed adverse losses are reversed and escalated to the Underwriting Manager.
Acceptance = documented review of loss activity and material risk change over the entire lapse window, with any adverse finding reflected in the reinstatement decision and terms.
Evidence in the GRC folder /underwriting/reinstatement/<policy-no>/, the claims platform loss-run and the PAS policy record.

Materiality/tolerance: any claim above the line-of-business large-loss threshold, any pattern of frequency, or a coverage-relevant risk change during the lapse is material and forces referral; minor sub-threshold items are noted only.
Effective dates: review window = lapse date through reinstatement request date; only losses with a date-of-loss inside this window are assessed for the reinstatement decision.

Field definitions from the claims data dictionary: claim_number, date_of_loss, incurred_amount, claim_status, cause_of_loss. Control total = count and incurred value of in-window claims reconcile between the loss-run and the review memo with 0 variance.

Counter-proposals below the floor are logged as pricing-deviation exceptions with disposition (accept within authority / refer for deviation approval / decline-and-non-renew) in the underwriting workstation and routed per the authority matrix.
The renewal pricing model/floor methodology is the approved production version; the rate-adequacy and technical-floor calculation uses the change-controlled model version cited on the assessment.
Sensitivity: the assessment shows the loss-ratio and combined-ratio impact of accepting the counter-proposal versus holding the floor, flagging cases where acceptance breaches the target loss ratio.

Materiality: a counter-proposal more than the authorized deviation percentage below the floor is material and requires Head of Pricing/CUO deviation approval; within-tolerance differences are handled at underwriter authority.
Quarterly sample of 25 renewal counter-proposal assessments drawn from the renewal negotiation log for the quarter.

PASS = counter-proposal compared to the correct technical floor, recommendation within authority or properly referred, and rationale documented; FAIL = no floor comparison, below-floor acceptance without approval, or missing rationale. Target >= 95%.
Below-floor acceptances without approval are unwound or ratified through deviation sign-off within 2 business days; repeat breaches escalate to the Underwriting Manager and Head of Pricing.

Acceptance = each counter-proposal has a documented comparison to the technical floor, a recommendation within authority (or an approved deviation), and rate-adequacy support before a renewal position is communicated to the broker.
Evidence in the GRC folder /underwriting/renewal/<account-no>/, the actuarial modeling platform output and the account record.

checklist.step: Apply the authority matrix to any deviation from the floor
checklist.value: Accepting a counter-proposal below the technical/filed floor requires deviation approval at the authority level tied to the deviation size.

testing.value: 100% of sampled below-floor acceptances have a documented deviation approval at the correct authority level; 0 unauthorized below-floor renewals.

checklist.step: Base the floor on correctly applied filed rates
checklist.value: The technical/renewal floor is derived from the current filed rates and rating factors for the risk, not ad-hoc figures.

testing.value: Sampled assessments show the floor computed from the current filed rating with the rate version cited; 0 floors using superseded rates.

checklist.step: Test the counter-proposal against loss-ratio targets
checklist.value: The assessment shows the projected loss ratio of the counter-proposal against the line-of-business target before a recommendation is made.

testing.value: 100% of sampled assessments document the projected loss ratio versus target; acceptances breaching target show an approved rationale.

answers.value: Confirmation that firm binding instructions (order to bind the renewal/placement) are received from the broker before the quote/renewal expiry, and validated against the agreed terms; scope = one placement/renewal per case, tracked in PAS and the CRM.
Binding instructions must be received before the quote validity/renewal expiry date; the confirmation window closes at expiry and any instruction after expiry requires re-quote or extension.

Broker identity/authority, policy/quote reference, agreed premium and terms, requested effective date and receipt timestamp of the binding instruction are populated and valid; instructions that vary from the quoted terms are flagged before binding.

The binding instruction reconciles to the firm quote: premium, limits, deductibles and effective date on the instruction match the quoted terms in PAS; any variance blocks bind until re-confirmed, with 0 tolerance on premium/limit mismatch.
The binding instruction (email/portal message) and the terms match check are stored in the CRM and on the PAS record and GRC folder /underwriting/renewal/<account-no>/ with timestamp and version.

Instructions received after expiry, or varying from quoted terms, are logged as exceptions in the underwriting workstation with disposition (re-quote / extend validity / decline) and routed to the Senior Underwriter for authority to bind.
Pre/post check: the bound policy record in PAS is compared to the firm quote and the binding instruction; premium, limits, terms and effective date match on all three before the policy is issued.
The bind is linked to the underwriting case/change record in PAS and the CRM opportunity, cross-referencing the quote reference and the binding instruction message id.
Quarterly sample of 25 bound renewals/placements drawn from the PAS bind register for the quarter.

PASS = binding instruction received before expiry, matched to quoted terms, and bound by an authorized underwriter; FAIL = bound after expiry without extension, term mismatch, or unauthorized bind. Target >= 99%.
Failures trigger correction/endorsement or re-quote within 2 business days; binds executed after expiry or outside authority are escalated to the Underwriting Manager and reviewed for E&O exposure.

Effective dating: the requested effective date on the binding instruction is validated against the quote validity; no cover is bound with an effective date before the instruction is confirmed and premium terms agreed.

Acceptance = binding instruction confirmed before expiry and matched to quoted terms, with an authorized bind and the instruction, quote and bound record all reconciling. Evidence: the binding instruction and terms-match check stored in the CRM and PAS, linked in the GRC folder /underwriting/renewal/<account-no>/.

checklist.step: Bind only on authorized instructions
checklist.value: Cover is bound only after a firm binding instruction is confirmed and only by an underwriter with binding authority for the risk.

testing.value: 100% of sampled binds show a confirmed binding instruction and an authorized underwriter; 0 unauthorized or instruction-less binds.

checklist.step: Document verbal or informal binding instructions within 24 hours
checklist.value: Any verbal/phone binding instruction is confirmed in writing and filed within 24 hours before or immediately after bind.

testing.value: Sampled binds originating from verbal instructions show written confirmation filed within 24 hours on 100% of cases.

checklist.step: Ensure the quote reached the broker ahead of expiry
checklist.value: The firm renewal quote underlying the binding instruction was delivered to the broker in advance of expiry so instructions can be confirmed in time.

testing.value: Sampled bound renewals show the quote issued to the broker before expiry with adequate lead time; late-quote cases are flagged.

checklist.step: Screen the insured before binding
checklist.value: Before confirming binding instructions and binding cover, the insured and relevant parties are screened against OFAC sanctions lists; a clear result is required to bind.

testing.value: 100% of sampled binds show a documented OFAC screening result dated before the bind; any hit shows a blocked/escalated disposition and no cover bound.

answers.value: Documentation of the lost-renewal reason for each non-retained account (declined, lost to competitor, non-renewed by carrier, insured cancelled), captured in a structured reason-code taxonomy; scope = all non-retained renewal accounts in the period.
The renewal period being closed out (monthly/quarterly retention cycle); a lost-reason must be recorded for every account that reaches its expiry without renewing in that cycle.

Account id, expiring premium, lost-reason code, competitor/price detail (where known) and free-text narrative are populated and valid in the CRM/PAS renewal record; a non-retained account without a reason code is flagged as incomplete.

The count of lost-reason records reconciles to the count of non-retained accounts for the period: every account with status Not-Renewed has exactly one reason code; delta between the non-retained list and the reason-coded list = 0.
The lost-renewal register (reason codes plus narratives) is retained in the CRM and exported to the GRC folder /underwriting/renewal/lost/<period>/ with timestamp and version for retention analytics.

Accounts marked lost without a reason, or with an ambiguous/other code lacking narrative, are logged as data-quality exceptions and returned to the owning underwriter for completion before the period closes.

checklist.step: Feed lost reasons into the win-back process
checklist.value: Documented lost-renewal reasons populate the win-back backlog so recoverable accounts (e.g. lost on price) can be targeted for re-approach.

testing.value: Sampled lost accounts with a recoverable reason code appear on the win-back list with a follow-up owner and date.

checklist.step: Use lost reasons to track retention against targets
checklist.value: Lost-reason data is aggregated by segment and compared to retention-rate targets to inform renewal strategy.

testing.value: The period retention report reconciles non-retained accounts to reason-coded records with 0 uncoded losses; segment retention is reported against target.

checklist.step: Document the lost-renewal reason in the account file
checklist.value: Each non-retained account file carries a reason code and supporting narrative rather than an unexplained lapse.

testing.value: 25-account quarterly sample shows a documented lost-reason code and narrative on 100% of non-retained accounts.
